{{Short description|Phenomenon of isolated many-body quantum systems not reaching thermal equilibrium}}
{{Use American English|date=January 2019}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=January 2019}}
{{Textbook|date=January 2021}}
'''Many-body localization (MBL)''' is a dynamical phenomenon occurring in isolated [[many-body]] quantum systems. It is characterized by the system failing to [[thermalization|reach thermal equilibrium]], and retaining a memory of its [[initial condition]] in local observables for infinite times.<ref name="NandkishoreHuse2015">{{cite journal|last1=Nandkishore|first1=Rahul|last2=Huse|first2=David A.|title=Many-Body Localization and Thermalization in Quantum Statistical Mechanics|journal=Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics|volume=6|issue=1|year=2015|pages=15–38|issn=1947-5454|doi=10.1146/annurev-conmatphys-031214-014726|arxiv=1404.0686|bibcode=2015ARCMP...6...15N|s2cid=118465889}}</ref>

== Thermalization and localization ==

Textbook [[quantum statistical mechanics]]<ref>Sakurai JJ. 1985. [[Modern Quantum Mechanics]]. Menlo Park, CA: Benjamin/Cummings</ref> assumes that systems go to thermal equilibrium ([[thermalization]]). The process of thermalization erases local memory of the initial conditions. In textbooks, thermalization is ensured by coupling the system to an external environment or "reservoir," with which the system can exchange energy. What happens if the system is isolated from the environment, and evolves according to its own [[Schrödinger equation]]? Does the system still thermalize?

Quantum mechanical time evolution is unitary and formally preserves all information about the initial condition in the [[quantum state]] at all times. However, a quantum system generically contains a macroscopic number of degrees of freedom, but can only be probed through few-body measurements which are local in real space. The meaningful question then becomes whether accessible local measurements display thermalization.

This question can be formalized by considering the quantum mechanical density matrix {{mvar|ρ}} of the system. If the system is divided into a subregion {{mvar|A}} (the region being probed) and its complement {{mvar|B}} (everything else), then all information that can be extracted by measurements made on {{mvar|A}} alone is encoded in the reduced density matrix <math>\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho(t)</math>. If, in the long time limit, <math>\rho_A(t)</math> approaches a thermal [[density matrix]] at a temperature set by the energy density in the state, then the system has "thermalized," and no local information about the initial condition can be extracted from local measurements. This process of "quantum thermalization" may be understood in terms of {{mvar|B}} acting as a reservoir for {{mvar|A}}. In this perspective, the entanglement entropy <math>S=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_A \log \rho_A)</math> of a thermalizing system in a pure state plays the role of thermal entropy.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Deutsch |first1=J M |title=Thermodynamic entropy of a many-body energy eigenstate |journal=New Journal of Physics |date=26 July 2010 |volume=12 |issue=7 |article-number=075021 |doi=10.1088/1367-2630/12/7/075021|arxiv=0911.0056 |s2cid=119180376 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Santos |first1=Lea F. |last2=Polkovnikov |first2=Anatoli |last3=Rigol |first3=Marcos |title=Weak and strong typicality in quantum systems |journal=Physical Review E |date=5 July 2012 |volume=86 |issue=1 |article-number=010102 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.86.010102|pmid=23005351 |doi-access=free |arxiv=1202.4764 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Deutsch |first1=J. M. |last2=Li |first2=Haibin |last3=Sharma |first3=Auditya |title=Microscopic origin of thermodynamic entropy in isolated systems |journal=Physical Review E |date=30 April 2013 |volume=87 |issue=4 |article-number=042135 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.87.042135|pmid=23679399 |arxiv=1202.2403 |s2cid=699412 }}</ref> Thermalizing systems therefore generically have [[Intensive and extensive properties|extensive]] or "volume law" entanglement entropy at any non-zero temperature.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Garrison |first1=James R. |last2=Grover |first2=Tarun |title=Does a Single Eigenstate Encode the Full Hamiltonian? |journal=Physical Review X |date=30 April 2018 |volume=8 |issue=2 |article-number=021026 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevX.8.021026|doi-access=free |arxiv=1503.00729 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dymarsky |first1=Anatoly |last2=Lashkari |first2=Nima |last3=Liu |first3=Hong |title=Subsystem eigenstate thermalization hypothesis |journal=Physical Review E |date=25 January 2018 |volume=97 |issue=1 |article-number=012140 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.97.012140|pmid=29448325 |hdl=1721.1/114450 |hdl-access=free |arxiv=1611.08764 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Huang |first1=Yichen |title=Universal eigenstate entanglement of chaotic local Hamiltonians |journal=Nuclear Physics B |date=January 2019 |volume=938 |pages=594–604 |doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2018.09.013|doi-access=free |arxiv=1708.08607 }}</ref> They also generically obey the [[eigenstate thermalization hypothesis]] (ETH).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Deutsch |first1=J. M. |title=Quantum statistical mechanics in a closed system |journal=Physical Review A |date=1 February 1991 |volume=43 |issue=4 |pages=2046–2049 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.43.2046 |pmid=9905246 |bibcode=1991PhRvA..43.2046D|s2cid=40633146 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Srednicki |first1=Mark |title=Chaos and quantum thermalization |journal=Physical Review E |date=1 August 1994 |volume=50 |issue=2 |pages=888–901 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.50.888|pmid=9962049 |arxiv=cond-mat/9403051 |bibcode=1994PhRvE..50..888S |s2cid=16065583 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rigol |first1=Marcos |last2=Dunjko |first2=Vanja |last3=Olshanii |first3=Maxim |title=Thermalization and its mechanism for generic isolated quantum systems |journal=Nature |date=April 2008 |volume=452 |issue=7189 |pages=854–858 |doi=10.1038/nature06838 |pmid=18421349 |arxiv=0708.1324 |bibcode=2008Natur.452..854R|s2cid=4384040 }}</ref>

In contrast, if <math>\rho_A(T)</math> fails to approach a thermal density matrix even in the long time limit, and remains instead close to its initial condition <math>\rho_A(0)</math>, then the system retains forever a memory of its initial condition in local observables. This latter possibility is referred to as "many body localization," and involves {{mvar|B}} failing to act as a reservoir for {{mvar|A}}.  A system in a many body localized phase exhibits MBL, and continues to exhibit MBL even when subject to arbitrary local perturbations. Eigenstates of systems exhibiting MBL do not obey the ETH, and generically follow an "area law" for entanglement entropy (i.e. the entanglement entropy scales with the surface area of subregion {{mvar|A}}). A brief list of properties differentiating thermalizing and MBL systems is provided below.
* In thermalizing systems, a memory of initial conditions is not accessible in local observables at long times. In MBL systems, memory of initial conditions remains accessible in local observables at long times.
* In thermalizing systems, energy eigenstates obey ETH. In MBL systems, energy eigenstates do not obey ETH.
* In thermalizing systems, energy eigenstates have volume law entanglement entropy. In MBL systems, energy eigenstates have area law entanglement entropy.
* Thermalizing systems generically have non-zero thermal conductivity. MBL systems have zero thermal conductivity.
* Thermalizing systems have continuous local spectra. MBL systems have discrete local spectra.<ref name="NandkishoreGopalakrishnan2014">{{cite journal|last1=Nandkishore|first1=Rahul|last2=Gopalakrishnan|first2=Sarang|last3=Huse|first3=David A.|title=Spectral features of a many-body-localized system weakly coupled to a bath|journal=Physical Review B|volume=90|issue=6|year=2014|article-number=064203|issn=1098-0121|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.90.064203|arxiv=1402.5971|s2cid=118568500}}</ref>
* In thermalizing systems, entanglement entropy grows as a [[power law]] in time starting from low entanglement initial conditions.<ref name="KimHuse2013">{{cite journal|last1=Kim|first1=Hyungwon|last2=Huse|first2=David A.|title=Ballistic Spreading of Entanglement in a Diffusive Nonintegrable System|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=111|issue=12|year=2013|article-number=127205|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.127205|pmid=24093298|arxiv=1306.4306|s2cid=41548576}}</ref> In MBL systems, entanglement entropy grows logarithmically in time starting from low entanglement initial conditions.<ref name="ŽnidaričProsen2008">{{cite journal |last1=Žnidarič |first1=Marko |last2=Prosen |first2=Tomaž |last3=Prelovšek |first3=Peter |title=Many-body localization in the Heisenberg XXZ magnet in a random field |journal=Physical Review B |date=25 February 2008 |volume=77 |issue=6 |article-number=064426 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.77.064426|arxiv=0706.2539 |s2cid=119132600 }}</ref><ref name="BardarsonPollmann2012">{{cite journal|last1=Bardarson|first1=Jens H.|last2=Pollmann|first2=Frank|last3=Moore|first3=Joel E.|title=Unbounded Growth of Entanglement in Models of Many-Body Localization|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=109|issue=1|article-number=017202|year=2012|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.109.017202|pmid=23031128|doi-access=free|arxiv=1202.5532}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Huang |first1=Yichen |title=Entanglement dynamics in critical random quantum Ising chain with perturbations |journal=Annals of Physics |date=May 2017 |volume=380 |pages=224–227 |doi=10.1016/j.aop.2017.02.018|s2cid=44548875 |url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/75049/1/1611.04727.pdf }}</ref>
* In thermalizing systems, the dynamics of out-of-time-ordered correlators forms a linear [[light cone]] which reflects the ballistic propagation of information. In MBL systems, the light cone is logarithmic.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Huang |first1=Yichen |last2=Zhang |first2=Yong-Liang |last3=Chen |first3=Xie |title=Out-of-time-ordered correlators in many-body localized systems |journal=Annalen der Physik |date=July 2017 |volume=529 |issue=7 |article-number=1600318 |doi=10.1002/andp.201600318|s2cid=42690831 |url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/72003/1/1608.01091v2.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fan |first1=Ruihua |last2=Zhang |first2=Pengfei |last3=Shen |first3=Huitao |last4=Zhai |first4=Hui |title=Out-of-time-order correlation for many-body localization |journal=Science Bulletin |date=May 2017 |volume=62 |issue=10 |pages=707–711 |doi=10.1016/j.scib.2017.04.011|doi-access=free |arxiv=1608.01914 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=He |first1=Rong-Qiang |last2=Lu |first2=Zhong-Yi |title=Characterizing many-body localization by out-of-time-ordered correlation |journal=Physical Review B |date=10 February 2017 |volume=95 |issue=5 |article-number=054201 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.95.054201|arxiv=1608.03586 |s2cid=119268185 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Swingle |first1=Brian |last2=Chowdhury |first2=Debanjan |title=Slow scrambling in disordered quantum systems |journal=Physical Review B |date=21 February 2017 |volume=95 |issue=6 |article-number=060201 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.95.060201|hdl=1721.1/107244 |s2cid=53485500 |hdl-access=free |arxiv=1608.03280 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chen |first1=Xiao |last2=Zhou |first2=Tianci |last3=Huse |first3=David A. |last4=Fradkin |first4=Eduardo |title=Out-of-time-order correlations in many-body localized and thermal phases |journal=Annalen der Physik |date=July 2017 |volume=529 |issue=7 |article-number=1600332 |doi=10.1002/andp.201600332|arxiv=1610.00220 |s2cid=119201477 }}</ref>

== History ==

MBL was first proposed by P.W. Anderson in 1958<ref name="Anderson1958">{{cite journal|last1=Anderson|first1=P. W.|title=Absence of Diffusion in Certain Random Lattices|journal=Physical Review|volume=109|issue=5|year=1958|pages=1492–1505|issn=0031-899X|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.109.1492|bibcode=1958PhRv..109.1492A}}</ref> as a possibility that could arise in strongly disordered quantum systems. The basic idea was that if particles all live in a random energy landscape, then any rearrangement of particles would change the energy of the system. Since energy is a conserved quantity in quantum mechanics, such a process can only be virtual and cannot lead to any transport of [[particle number]] or energy.

While localization for single particle systems was demonstrated already in Anderson's original paper (coming to be known as [[Anderson localization]]), the existence of the phenomenon for many particle systems remained a conjecture for decades. In 1980 Fleishman and Anderson<ref name="FleishmanAnderson1980">{{cite journal|last1=Fleishman|first1=L.|last2=Anderson|first2=P. W.|title=Interactions and the Anderson transition|journal=Physical Review B|volume=21|issue=6|year=1980|pages=2366–2377|issn=0163-1829|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.21.2366}}</ref> demonstrated the phenomenon survived the addition of interactions to lowest order in [[perturbation theory]]. In a 1998 study,<ref name="AltshulerGefen1997">{{cite journal|last1=Altshuler|first1=Boris L.|last2=Gefen|first2=Yuval|last3=Kamenev|first3=Alex|last4=Levitov|first4=Leonid S.|title=Quasiparticle Lifetime in a Finite System: A Nonperturbative Approach|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=78|issue=14|year=1997|pages=2803–2806|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.2803|arxiv=cond-mat/9609132|bibcode=1997PhRvL..78.2803A|s2cid=18852288}}</ref> the analysis was extended to all orders in perturbation theory, in a [[zero-dimensional system]], and the MBL phenomenon was shown to survive. In 2005<ref name="GornyiMirlin2005">{{cite journal|last1=Gornyi|first1=I. V.|last2=Mirlin|first2=A. D.|last3=Polyakov|first3=D. G.|title=Interacting Electrons in Disordered Wires: Anderson Localization and Low-T Transport|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=95|issue=20|year=2005|article-number=206603|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.206603|pmid=16384079|arxiv=cond-mat/0506411|s2cid=39376817}}</ref> and 2006,<ref name="BaskoAleiner2006">{{cite journal|last1=Basko|first1=D.M.|last2=Aleiner|first2=I.L.|last3=Altshuler|first3=B.L.|title=Metal–insulator transition in a weakly interacting many-electron system with localized single-particle states|journal=Annals of Physics|volume=321|issue=5|year=2006|pages=1126–1205|issn=0003-4916|doi=10.1016/j.aop.2005.11.014|arxiv=cond-mat/0506617|bibcode=2006AnPhy.321.1126B|s2cid=18345541}}</ref> this was extended to high orders in perturbation theory in high dimensional systems. MBL was argued to survive at least at low energy density. A series of numerical works<ref name="OganesyanHuse2007">{{cite journal|last1=Oganesyan|first1=Vadim|last2=Huse|first2=David A.|title=Localization of interacting fermions at high temperature|journal=Physical Review B|volume=75|issue=15|year=2007|article-number=155111|issn=1098-0121|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.75.155111|arxiv=cond-mat/0610854|s2cid=119488834}}</ref><ref name="ŽnidaričProsen2008"/><ref name="PalHuse2010">{{cite journal|last1=Pal|first1=Arijeet|last2=Huse|first2=David A.|title=Many-body localization phase transition|journal=Physical Review B|volume=82|issue=17|year=2010|article-number=174411|issn=1098-0121|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.82.174411|arxiv=1010.1992|s2cid=41528861}}</ref>
<ref name="SerbynPapić2014">{{cite journal|last1=Serbyn|first1=Maksym|last2=Papić|first2=Z.|last3=Abanin|first3=D. A.|title=Quantum quenches in the many-body localized phase|journal=Physical Review B|volume=90|issue=17|year=2014|article-number=174302 |issn=1098-0121|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.90.174302|hdl=1721.1/91499|s2cid=18658716|hdl-access=free|arxiv=1408.4105}}</ref> provided further evidence for the phenomenon in one dimensional systems, at all energy densities ("infinite temperature"). Finally, in 2014<ref name="Imbrie2016">{{cite journal|last1=Imbrie|first1=John Z.|title=On Many-Body Localization for Quantum Spin Chains|journal=Journal of Statistical Physics|volume=163|issue=5|year=2016|pages=998–1048|issn=0022-4715|doi=10.1007/s10955-016-1508-x|arxiv=1403.7837|s2cid=11250762}}</ref> Imbrie presented a proof of MBL for certain one dimensional spin chains with strong disorder, with the localization being stable to arbitrary local perturbations – i.e. the systems were shown to be in a many body localized phase.

It is now believed that MBL can arise also in periodically driven "Floquet" systems where energy is conserved only modulo the drive frequency.<ref name="D'AlessioPolkovnikov2013">{{cite journal|last1=D'Alessio|first1=Luca|last2=Polkovnikov|first2=Anatoli|title=Many-body energy localization transition in periodically driven systems|journal=Annals of Physics|volume=333|year=2013|pages=19–33|issn=0003-4916|doi=10.1016/j.aop.2013.02.011|arxiv=1210.2791|s2cid=118476386}}</ref><ref name="LazaridesDas2015">{{cite journal|last1=Lazarides|first1=Achilleas|last2=Das|first2=Arnab|last3=Moessner|first3=Roderich|title=Fate of Many-Body Localization Under Periodic Driving|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=115|issue=3|year=2015|article-number=030402|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.115.030402|pmid=26230771|arxiv=1410.3455|s2cid=28538293}}</ref><ref name="PontePapić2015">{{cite journal|last1=Ponte|first1=Pedro|last2=Papić|first2=Z.|last3=Huveneers|first3=François|last4=Abanin|first4=Dmitry A.|title=Many-Body Localization in Periodically Driven Systems|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=114|issue=14|year=2015|article-number=140401|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.114.140401|pmid=25910094|s2cid=38608177|url=http://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/88190/7/PapicMany-bodylocalization.pdf}}</ref>

In 2025,<ref name="AzodiRabitz2025">{{cite journal | last1 = Azodi | first1 = Peyman | last2 = Rabitz | first2 = Herschel A.
 | title = Stability and quasi-periodicity of many-body localized dynamics | journal = New Journal of Physics | volume = 27 | issue = 7 | year = 2025 | pages = 074506 | publisher = IOP Publishing | doi = 10.1088/1367-2630/adedae | url = https://doi.org/10.1088/1367-2630/adedae| doi-access = free }}</ref> showed that subsystems within many-body localized systems follow stable quasi-periodic dynamics rather than approaching a steady, thermalized state. The work further showed that averaging over many disorder realizations—an approach commonly used in the literature—can mask this behavior and produce the misleading appearance of slow, logarithmic entanglement growth, even though individual subsystems do not thermalize. This result provides a new evidence for the stability of the MBL phase. 
== Emergent integrability ==

Many body localized systems exhibit a phenomenon known as emergent integrability. In a non-interacting Anderson insulator, the occupation number of each localized single particle orbital is separately a local integral of motion. It was conjectured<ref name="SerbynPapić2013">{{cite journal|last1=Serbyn|first1=Maksym|last2=Papić|first2=Z.|last3=Abanin|first3=Dmitry A.|title=Local Conservation Laws and the Structure of the Many-Body Localized States|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=111|issue=12|year=2013|article-number=127201|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.127201|pmid=24093294|arxiv=1305.5554|s2cid=13006260}}</ref><ref name="HuseNandkishore2014">{{cite journal|last1=Huse|first1=David A.|last2=Nandkishore|first2=Rahul|last3=Oganesyan|first3=Vadim|title=Phenomenology of fully many-body-localized systems|journal=Physical Review B|volume=90|issue=17|year=2014|article-number=174202|issn=1098-0121|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.90.174202|arxiv=1305.4915|s2cid=5553355}}</ref> (and proven by Imbrie) that a similar extensive set of local integrals of motion should also exist in the MBL phase. Consider for specificity a one dimensional spin-1/2 chain with Hamiltonian

:<math>H=\sum_i \left [ J \left ( X_i X_{i+1} + Y_i Y_{i+1} \right ) + J^\prime Z_i Z_{i+1} + h_i Z_i  \right ],</math>

where {{math|<var>X</var>}}, {{math|<var>Y</var>}} and {{math|<var>Z</var>}} are Pauli operators, and {{math|<var>h<sub>I</sub></var>}} are random variables drawn from a distribution of some width {{math|<var>W</var>}}. When the disorder is strong enough ({{math|<var>W</var>&gt;<var>W<sub>c</sub></var>}}) that all eigenstates are localized, then there exists a local unitary transformation to new variables {{math|<var>τ</var>}} such that

:<math>H=\sum_i h^\prime_i \tau^z_i + \sum_{ij} J_{ij} \tau^z_i \tau^z_j + \sum_{ijk} K_{ijk} \tau^z_i \tau^z_j \tau^z_k + \cdots,</math>

where {{math|<var>τ</var>}} are Pauli operators that are related to the physical Pauli operators by a local unitary transformation, the ... indicates additional terms which only involve {{math|<var>τ<sup>z</sup></var>}} operators, and the coefficients fall off exponentially with distance. This Hamiltonian manifestly contains an extensive number of localized integrals of motion or "l-bits" (the operators {{math|<var>τ<sup>z</sup><sub>i</sub></var>}}, which all commute with the Hamiltonian). If the original Hamiltonian is perturbed, the l-bits get redefined, but the integrable structure survives.

== Exotic orders ==

MBL enables the formation of exotic forms of quantum order that could not arise in thermal equilibrium, through the phenomenon of [[localization-protected quantum order]].<ref name="HuseNandkishore2013">{{cite journal|last1=Huse|first1=David A.|last2=Nandkishore|first2=Rahul|last3=Oganesyan|first3=Vadim|last4=Pal|first4=Arijeet|last5=Sondhi|first5=S. L.|title=Localization-protected quantum order|journal=Physical Review B|volume=88|issue=1|year=2013|article-number=014206|issn=1098-0121|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.88.014206|arxiv=1304.1158|bibcode=2013PhRvB..88a4206H|doi-access=free}}</ref> A form of localization-protected quantum order, arising only in periodically driven systems, is the Floquet [[time crystal]].<ref name="KhemaniLazarides2016">{{cite journal|last1=Khemani|first1=Vedika|last2=Lazarides|first2=Achilleas|last3=Moessner|first3=Roderich|last4=Sondhi|first4=S. L.|title=Phase Structure of Driven Quantum Systems|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=116|issue=25|year=2016|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.250401|pmid=27391704|article-number=250401|arxiv=1508.03344|doi-access=free|bibcode=2016PhRvL.116y0401K}}</ref><ref name="ElseBauer2016">{{cite journal|last1=Else|first1=Dominic V.|last2=Bauer|first2=Bela|last3=Nayak|first3=Chetan|title=Floquet Time Crystals|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=117|issue=9|year=2016|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.117.090402|arxiv=1603.08001|pmid=27610834|article-number=090402|bibcode=2016PhRvL.117i0402E|s2cid=1652633}}</ref><ref name="von KeyserlingkKhemani2016">{{cite journal|last1=von Keyserlingk|first1=C. W.|last2=Khemani|first2=Vedika|last3=Sondhi|first3=S. L.|title=Absolute stability and spatiotemporal long-range order in Floquet systems|journal=Physical Review B|volume=94|issue=8|year=2016|article-number=085112|issn=2469-9950|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.94.085112|arxiv=1605.00639|doi-access=free|bibcode=2016PhRvB..94h5112V}}</ref><ref name="ZhangHess2017">{{cite journal|last1=Zhang|first1=J.|last2=Hess|first2=P. W.|last3=Kyprianidis|first3=A.|last4=Becker|first4=P.|last5=Lee|first5=A.|last6=Smith|first6=J.|last7=Pagano|first7=G.|last8=Potirniche|first8=I.-D.|last9=Potter|first9=A. C.|last10=Vishwanath|first10=A.|last11=Yao|first11=N. Y.|last12=Monroe|first12=C.|title=Observation of a discrete time crystal|journal=Nature|volume=543|issue=7644|year=2017|pages=217–220|issn=0028-0836|doi=10.1038/nature21413|arxiv=1609.08684|pmid=28277505|bibcode=2017Natur.543..217Z|s2cid=4450646}}</ref><ref name="ChoiChoi2017">{{cite journal|last1=Choi|first1=Soonwon|last2=Choi|first2=Joonhee|last3=Landig|first3=Renate|last4=Kucsko|first4=Georg|last5=Zhou|first5=Hengyun|last6=Isoya|first6=Junichi|last7=Jelezko|first7=Fedor|last8=Onoda|first8=Shinobu|last9=Sumiya|first9=Hitoshi|last10=Khemani|first10=Vedika|last11=von Keyserlingk|first11=Curt|last12=Yao|first12=Norman Y.|last13=Demler|first13=Eugene|last14=Lukin|first14=Mikhail D.|title=Observation of discrete time-crystalline order in a disordered dipolar many-body system|journal=Nature|volume=543|issue=7644|year=2017|pages=221–225|issn=0028-0836|doi=10.1038/nature21426|pmc=5349499|pmid=28277511|arxiv=1610.08057|bibcode=2017Natur.543..221C}}</ref>

== Experimental realizations ==

A number of experiments have been reported observing the MBL phenomenon.<ref name="KondovMcGehee2015">{{cite journal|last1=Kondov|first1=S. S.|last2=McGehee|first2=W. R.|last3=Xu|first3=W.|last4=DeMarco|first4=B.|title=Disorder-Induced Localization in a Strongly Correlated Atomic Hubbard Gas|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=114|issue=8|year=2015|article-number=083002|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.114.083002|pmid=25768762|doi-access=free|arxiv=1305.6072}}</ref><ref name="SchreiberHodgman2015">{{cite journal|last1=Schreiber|first1=M.|last2=Hodgman|first2=S. S.|last3=Bordia|first3=P.|last4=Luschen|first4=H. P.|last5=Fischer|first5=M. H.|last6=Vosk|first6=R.|last7=Altman|first7=E.|last8=Schneider|first8=U.|last9=Bloch|first9=I.|title=Observation of many-body localization of interacting fermions in a quasirandom optical lattice|journal=Science|volume=349|issue=6250|year=2015|pages=842–845|issn=0036-8075|doi=10.1126/science.aaa7432|pmid=26229112|arxiv=1501.05661|s2cid=5112350}}</ref><ref name="ChoiHild2016">{{cite journal|last1=Choi|first1=J.-y.|last2=Hild|first2=S.|last3=Zeiher|first3=J.|last4=Schauss|first4=P.|last5=Rubio-Abadal|first5=A.|last6=Yefsah|first6=T.|last7=Khemani|first7=V.|last8=Huse|first8=D. A.|last9=Bloch|first9=I.|last10=Gross|first10=C.|title=Exploring the many-body localization transition in two dimensions|journal=Science|volume=352|issue=6293|year=2016|pages=1547–1552|issn=0036-8075|doi=10.1126/science.aaf8834|arxiv=1604.04178|pmid=27339981|bibcode=2016Sci...352.1547C|s2cid=35012132}}</ref><ref name="WeiRamanathan2018">{{cite journal|last1=Wei|first1=Ken Xuan|last2=Ramanathan|first2=Chandrasekhar|last3=Cappellaro|first3=Paola|title=Exploring Localization in Nuclear Spin Chains|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=120|issue=7|year=2018|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.070501|pmid=29542978|article-number=070501|doi-access=free|bibcode=2018PhRvL.120g0501W|arxiv=1612.05249}}</ref>  Most of these experiments involve synthetic quantum systems, such as assemblies of [[ultracold atom]]s or [[trapped ion]]s.<ref name="SmithLee2016">{{cite journal|last1=Smith|first1=J.|last2=Lee|first2=A.|last3=Richerme|first3=P.|last4=Neyenhuis|first4=B.|last5=Hess|first5=P. W.|last6=Hauke|first6=P.|last7=Heyl|first7=M.|last8=Huse|first8=D. A.|last9=Monroe|first9=C.|title=Many-body localization in a quantum simulator with programmable random disorder|journal=Nature Physics|volume=12|issue=10|year=2016|pages=907–911|issn=1745-2473|doi=10.1038/nphys3783|arxiv=1508.07026|bibcode=2016NatPh..12..907S|s2cid=53408060}}</ref> Experimental explorations of the phenomenon in solid state systems are still in their infancy.
